analysis.note: Ablatival pronoun used adverbially as an inferential connective; the commentary construes it with yasmāt.
Relative genitive singular; the commentary supplies the referent yateḥ, “of the ascetic.”
Vocative address, confirmed by the commentary’s he mahābāho.

verification.detail: compound stem mahābāhu as Pum/Sambodhana/Eka: pass; relation bahuvrihi: unsupported (logged)

analysis.note: Past passive participial adjective from ni + √grah; predicate to indriyāṇi, with asti understood.
Glossed by the commentary as sarva-prakāraiḥ mānasādi-bhedaiḥ, “by all modes, with distinctions beginning with the mental.”
Ablative plural of separation governed by nigṛhītāni; the commentary glosses these objects as śabda and the rest.

verification.detail: compound stem indriyārtha as Pum/Panchami/Bahu: pass; relation tatpurusa: unsupported (logged)

analysis.note: Subject of pratiṣṭhitā; in this context, wisdom as discriminative knowledge.
Feminine nominative singular participial/adjectival form, agreeing with prajñā; PPP of prati + √sthā, “established, firmly settled.”

justifications.decision: tasmāt is an inferential connective grounded in the fault already shown in the activity of the senses.
options_considered: ablatival “from that” as a local/separative phrase

evidence.quote: indriyāṇāṃ pravṛttau doṣa upapādito yasmāt tasmāt
evidence.translation: Because the defect in the activity of the senses has been demonstrated, therefore...

justifications.decision: The genitive relative-correlative construction is to be understood as “of the ascetic whose ... of that one.”
options_considered: a completely unspecified “whoever” with no supplied referent
reference to a yati, as supplied by the commentary
justifications.chosen: yasya/tasya refer to a yati, “ascetic/disciplined person.”

evidence.quote: yasya yateḥ he mahābāho, nigṛhītāni ... tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā
evidence.translation: of whose—the ascetic’s—O mighty-armed one, [the senses] are restrained ... that one’s wisdom is established.

justifications.decision: indriyārthebhyaḥ is ablative plural with nigṛhītāni; it means sense-objects, not “purposes” in the abstract.
options_considered: objects of the senses, with ablative separation
the senses actively restraining the objects
justifications.chosen: “restrained from the objects of the senses,” i.e. from sound and the rest.

evidence.translation: the senses restrained from the sense-objects, from sound and the rest.

justifications.decision: sarvaśaḥ modifies the restraint by specifying all modes or manners, not simply “all the senses.”
options_considered: “all the senses” as the scope of sarvaśaḥ
“in every way/by all modes,” as glossed
justifications.chosen: “in every way,” with modes including the mental.

evidence.translation: sarvaśaḥ: by all modes, with distinctions beginning with the mental.

justifications.decision: The word is not syntactically part of the yasya phrase; it directly addresses Arjuna.
options_considered: a descriptive compound belonging with yasya
justifications.chosen: mahābāho is a vocative address, “O mighty-armed one.”

justifications.decision: The verse’s formula tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā is read in the sthita-prajña context, where Śaṅkara characterizes the person as one in whom discriminative knowledge has arisen.
justifications.chosen: prajñā is “wisdom/discriminative knowledge,” and pratiṣṭhitā means “established, firmly settled.”

evidence.translation: of the person of established wisdom, whose discriminative knowledge has arisen.

translation: Therefore, O mighty-armed one, the wisdom (prajñā) of that ascetic whose senses are restrained in every way from the objects of the senses is firmly established.
one_shot_delta: A commentary-blind translation might render indriyārtha as “the purposes of the senses”; Śaṅkara’s gloss śabdādibhyas makes it “sense-objects,” such as sound (line 1).
It might take sarvaśaḥ as only “completely” or as referring vaguely to all the senses; the bhāṣya specifies “by all modes,” including mental distinctions (line 1).
It might miss that yasya is supplied with yateḥ: Śaṅkara understands the person as the disciplined ascetic whose senses are restrained (line 1).
It might treat tasmāt as a bare “from that”; Śaṅkara explicitly connects it to the previously shown defect in sense-activity, hence “therefore” (line 1).
analyzer_disagreements: ByT5 split mahā_bāho as mahat_Cp + bāhu_SVM; I analyze the printed expression as the compound stem mahābāhu, masculine vocative singular, a bahuvrīhi, as confirmed by the bhāṣya’s he mahābāho (line 1).
ByT5 segmented indriya_arthebhyaḥ; I analyze it as the compound stem indriyārtha, masculine ablative plural, glossed by śabdādibhyaḥ in the commentary (line 1).

ByT5 gave nigrah as the lemma for nigṛhītāni; since the required analysis is of the subanta actually inflected, I record the nominal participial stem nigṛhīta, neuter nominative plural, noting its derivation from ni + √grah.
ByT5 gave pratiṣṭhā for pratiṣṭhitā; I analyze the form as feminine nominative singular of the participial/adjectival stem pratiṣṭhitā, agreeing with prajñā, not as the abstract noun pratiṣṭhā.
mula: tasmād yasya mahābāho nigṛhītāni sarvaśaḥ | indriyāṇīndriyārthebhyas tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā
commentary_lines: indriyāṇāṃ pravṛttau doṣa upapādito yasmāt tasmāt yasya yateḥ he mahābāho, nigṛhītāni sarvaśaḥ sarva-prakāraiḥ mānasādi-bhedaiḥ indriyāṇi indriyārthebhyaḥ śabdādibhyas tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā ||bhgs_2.68||
